program: ODSP income support: treatment of income (Directive 5.1, April 2026). Earnings exemptions live in Directive 5.3 and are NOT yet extracted.
status: DRAFT: written by Claude from the directive text. Not yet reviewed by a human.

rules.quote: Income is deducted from ODSP income support unless partially or fully exempt by regulation.
Applicants/recipients must demonstrate reasonable efforts to obtain any financial resources to which they or their dependants may be entitled, within a reasonable timeframe.

Applicants and recipients are not required to apply for early retirement pension from CPP. However, ODSP applicants who choose to apply for and receive early retirement pensions will have these funds deducted from their income support.
ODSP applicants/recipients are required to pursue OAS when they turn 65. Income from OAS is deducted dollar for dollar from income support.
Applicants with dependent children who are eligible to receive the Ontario Child Benefit (OCB) and Canada Child Benefit (CCB) must demonstrate reasonable efforts to obtain these financial resources.

Income includes ... wages, salaries, casual earnings ...; business income; pension/superannuation/insurance benefit payments; annuity payments; mortgage payments received; foreign pensions; spousal support; Employment Insurance; Old Age Security and Guaranteed Income Supplement; Ontario Guaranteed Annual Income Act; WSIB/Workers' Compensation loss-of-income benefits; Pension Act (Canada); War Veterans Allowance.
60% of gross income for renting self-contained quarters, land or a garage;
rules.note: The same directive also says '40% of gross rental income, and 60% of gross board and lodging income' in the exemptions list, which is the same split read from the other side (40% exempt).

rules.quote: Roomer income is charged at 60% of the amount paid or $100, whichever is greater.
Boarder income is charged at 40% of the amount paid or $100, whichever is greater.
rules.note: Roomer = lodging without meals; boarder = lodging with meals.

rules.quote: There is no income charge if an ODSP applicant, recipient, or spouse provides board and lodging or rents to a child or grandchild who is receiving ODSP or Ontario Works in their own right.

An amount up to $10,000 in a 12 month period per member of the benefit unit, in the form of gifts or voluntary payments for any purpose from any source; (this includes monies from trusts, life insurance policies, honorariums and windfalls).

Payments from any source in the form of gifts or voluntary payments used for disability-related items and services or for education and training incurred because of the disability of a member of the benefit unit. There is no limit on the value of these contributions, provided they will not be reimbursed from other sources.

Gifts or voluntary payments that will be applied to the purchase of a principal residence, an exempt vehicle, or that will be applied to the first and last month's rent necessary to secure accommodation.
a cash bonus from an employer given in consideration for services rendered or work performed, does not qualify for this exemption.

Refundable tax credits including the: Canada Child Tax Benefit; Canada Child Benefit; Ontario Children's Activity Tax Credit; Ontario Trillium Benefit payment; Ontario Child Benefit (OCB) payments ...
Child support (Effective January 1, 2017).
the Canada Workers Benefit (CWB), formerly the Working Income Tax Benefit (WITB) ...
A Canada Disability Benefit payment under the Canada Disability Benefit Act.
All payments made under the Canada-Ontario Housing Benefit (COHB) program (e.g., housing allowances, payments for first/last month's rent).

RDSP related exemptions: gifts or voluntary contributions made to RDSPs by family members and other third parties; interest earned on and re-invested in an RDSP; the federal Canada Disability Savings Grants and Canada Disability Savings Bonds; and all withdrawals from an RDSP for any purpose.
All donations received from a religious, charitable or benevolent organization for any purpose;
All payments received for activities related to participating in a jury.
Earnings of dependent children;
Interest earned on liquid assets up to the prescribed asset limits, e.g. $40,000 for a single recipient;
Payments from Ontario Works employment assistance;
Payments received under the Ontario Autism Program for autism services and supports;

Funds received from the Ministry of College and Universities or Canada Student Financial Assistance for education costs such as books, tuition, instructional supplies, transportation costs, child care and compulsory fees;

Proceeds from a court judgement or legal settlement or an award from a statutory tribunal ... received as damages or compensation for pain and suffering, due to injury to or the death of a member of the benefit unit.
This does not apply to a WSIB NEL award that provides compensation for the physical, functional or psychological loss suffered from permanent impairment caused by a work-related injury or illness.
CAS payments made to a recipient for providing care to a foster child are exempt as income.

The value of all grants, payments, credits, services or items provided by Ontario utilities and regulators, municipalities, and the Governments of Ontario or Canada, for the purposes of energy efficiency, conservation or affordability, are exempt as income for social assistance purposes.

Arts grants awarded to any member of the benefit unit are to be exempt as income and assets ... The portion of the grant that provides living costs (for example funds intended to help with shelter costs) is to be considered income.
Severance pay is treated as income in the month it is received and earnings exemptions do not apply.

Money received from the sale of an asset is income in the month received if not otherwise exempt. There is no income charge ... for that portion of a payment ... that is applied or with approval, will be used to purchase: a principal residence; any other approved asset that is necessary for health or welfare; or an exempt asset.
In general, a conversion of non-exempt or exempt assets should be within a six month time frame.

Loans including a reverse mortgage used for an approved purpose. Approved purposes include: the purchase of approved disability-related items or services; expenses for health-related reasons as supported by a medical doctor, and approved by the Director; business loans; ... loans for the payment of first and last month's rent; loans for the purchase of normal household items.

the ODSP requirement that applicants and recipients pursue all available resources as a condition of eligibility is NOT applicable to locked-in retirement accounts. However, if an ODSP recipient does access these funds, ODSP rules regarding income and assets must be applied.

flags_for_human_review: Earnings exemptions (the single biggest factor for working recipients) are in Directive 5.3, not 5.1. Not yet extracted, so the screener cannot compute net benefit for anyone with employment income.
Directive 5.1 contains stale locked-in funds figures ($31,466.67 and $18,880, both 2010). Do not use.
The amount of the monthly ODSP benefit (Directive 6.x) is not extracted, so we cannot say what remains after deductions.

Rent: 5.1 lists '60% of gross income for renting self-contained quarters' as charged and also '40% of gross rental income, and 60% of gross board and lodging income' under exemptions. Read together they say 60% of rent is charged; the board and lodging wording under exemptions conflicts with the roomer (60%) and boarder (40%) rules above. Needs a caseworker to confirm.
The list of charged income includes 'Employment Insurance Act (Canada)' but the text also says EI amounts are deducted gross less earnings deduction. Interaction with 5.3 needs checking.
Many exemptions depend on the Director's approval or on how funds are used (disability-related, housing, trust reporting). These must answer 'unclear, ask a caseworker'.
Other directives referenced and not yet read: 5.2, 5.3, 5.4 (self-employment), 5.5 (child care), 5.8 (gifts), 5.9, 5.10, 5.11, 5.15 (support), 5.18.
